items.title: Literary Translators Warn AI Threatens Their Livelihoods in Copyright Case
items.excerpt: The American Literary Translators Association and 11 other creative-professional groups filed an amicus brief in the Authors Guild v. OpenAI/Microsoft case, warning AI translation could turn translators 'from interpreters into primarily editors of large language model outputs.' Note: OpenAI MDL amicus angle was deprioritized; this is the translators-specific brief.

items.title: AI Training is Copyright Infringement: What Publishers Need to Know about Thomson Reuters v ROSS Intelligence
items.excerpt: Analysis of the Third Circuit's ROSS opinion for publishers: the more an AI product is marketed as solving research challenges, the less transformative its use of STM content becomes. Follow-up to the ROSS decision covered 10-06; this is the publisher-licensing takeaway piece.

items.title: The Anatomy of 'Harm': An Interview with IFRRO CEO Anita Huss-Ekerhult on AI and Copyright
items.excerpt: IFRRO's CEO explains its study quantifying economic harm from generative AI to authors and publishers, and how an AI licensing market is already emerging through collective management organisations.

items.title: Can this golden audio era deliver on its potential?
items.excerpt: Ahead of the British Audio Awards, audiobook executives (Bonnier, Libro.fm and others) discuss how AI is reshaping production workflows and driving 'audio content inflation' as production costs fall, alongside discoverability and pricing pressure.

items.title: AI is giving writers the support publishing cannot
items.excerpt: Comment: Marian Stan argues AI tools now give aspiring novelists the editorial feedback that traditional publishing has long failed to provide. (Opinion piece; specific to AI manuscript feedback.)

items.title: Publishing Ireland conference: AI and rising costs high on the agenda
items.excerpt: Publishing Ireland's annual autumn conference, overseen by president-elect Jonathan Creasy, tackled AI alongside rising costs across the book trade. (Body mostly paywalled; AI depth unverified.)

items.title: More AI Prompts Found in Journal Papers
items.excerpt: Blatant LLM instructions such as 'write a positive review' left in published papers are the starkest sign yet that authors are trying to game AI-assisted peer review, scholars warn.

items.title: 'AI Slop' Papers Published Under Prominent Academics' Names
items.excerpt: High-profile researchers were listed as authors of AI-generated papers in little-known journals, raising concern that Ph.D. students could be lured into submitting there too.

items.title: [윤주혜의 C] 투고 쏟아지고 문학상 응모 최다…AI가 불붙인 '딸깍 출판'
items.excerpt: AI가 써준 200쪽 원고와 돈만 있으면 책을 낼 수 있는 '딸깍 출판' 시대 — 출판사 투고와 문학상 응모가 역대 최다로 몰리며 출판계가 AI 원고 판별에 부담을 겪고 있다는 칼럼. (11-18 ajunews AI 원고 급증 카드의 후속/칼럼이라 중복 가능성 있음.)

items.title: Tamil Nadu library scam: Publisher who 'supplied' fake books under fictitious names arrested
items.excerpt: Vigilance officers arrested R Mohan of Agalvilakku Publishers and Phoenix Publications, which received Rs 1.74 crore for supplying allegedly AI-generated books under fictitious author names to Tamil Nadu public libraries. Off-list outlet; new development (arrest) after the probe covered 11-07.

items.title: 잉크플록, 한국 웹소설 해외 유통을 위한 AI 현지화 체계 개발
items.excerpt: 스타트업 잉크플록이 한국 웹소설을 해외에 유통하기 위한 AI 기반 번역·현지화 체계를 개발했다. Off-list outlet (on-list Korean outlets had no item).

items.title: 장성 주민 15명, AI로 전자그림책 작가 데뷔
items.excerpt: 전남 장성군 주민 15명이 생성형 AI를 활용해 자신만의 이야기를 전자그림책으로 출판하며 디지털 창작자로 데뷔했다. Off-list outlet.

items.title: AI 학습에 내 책이 쓰인다면? 출판계 저작권 보호·지원 법안 본격 시동
items.excerpt: 윤용근 의원 등 14인이 발의한 '출판문화산업 진흥법' 개정안이 11월 16~25일 입법예고되는 가운데, 출판물의 AI 학습 이용과 권리자 동의·보호 체계가 쟁점으로 떠올랐다. (셀렉트스타·출협 협약 부분은 기보도.) Off-list outlet.

items.title: “AI 저작권 규제해도, 안 해도 문제”... 세계 도서관계, 법적 공백·과잉 규제 동시 경고
items.excerpt: 국제도서관협회연맹(IFLA)이 각국 생성형 AI 저작권 입법 현황을 조사해, AI 학습·권리자 보호 정책이 엇갈리며 도서관 연구지원과 지식 접근권이 흔들릴 수 있다고 경고하고 명확한 지침을 촉구했다. Off-list outlet.

items.title: How Much AI-Generated Text Is In Today's Philosophy Journals? (guest post)
items.excerpt: A guest analysis runs AI-text detection across recent philosophy journal articles and finds philosophers have started making substantial use of AI, with AI-generated passages not uncommon in published papers. Off-list outlet.

items.title: Celebrity ghostwriters are now selling points, not secrets. Is AI a factor?
items.excerpt: Once hidden, the writers behind celebrity memoirs are now credited as a selling point; the piece argues that in an age of AI, a named human collaborator may serve as a mark of authenticity. Off-list outlet.

items.title: Professor Mark Green receives payout in massive AI copyright settlement
items.excerpt: Simpson College professor Mark Green received a payout from the $1.5B Bartz v. Anthropic settlement for his textbook 'Global Marketing' — an early first-hand confirmation of payments reaching authors. Off-list student paper; time is date-only (body: November 18, 2026). Bartz follow-up rule applies.

items.title: 'Ahead of his time': AI helps unlock discoveries hidden in notebooks of man who transformed maths
items.excerpt: Kurt Gödel left 1,009 pages of shorthand notebooks; AI-assisted transcription is now helping scholars decode them and surface overlooked ideas — an archival/manuscript use of AI.
